extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors submitting synopses to literary agents (fiction, memoir, nonfiction writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a book synopsis to submit to literary agents, covering length, format, plot, characters, tense, style, and other practical considerations for fiction, memoir, and nonfiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A book synopsis is a summary of your book that helps readers understand what your book is about and why they should want to read it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize both what the book is about (content) and why it matters (appeal). The synopsis is a tool agents/editors use to judge professionalism and decide whether to read the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length — Fiction / Memoir / Narrative Nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Create two versions: the short version should be 1-2 pages; the long version should be approximately 1 synopsis page for every 25 pages of manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the short version to book agents unless they specifically ask for the long version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length — Nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Create two versions for nonfiction: a short version of 1-2 paragraphs and a long version of 1-2 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the short version in your query letter and the long version in your book proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the synopsis is double-spaced and paragraphs are indented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot (for novelists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information about your plot and subplots, thinking of plot as the external events that take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not delve into subplots unless they directly affect the central plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey the themes that drive your book — the reasons the book matters and makes readers feel something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether fiction or nonfiction, include themes because they explain why the book matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending / Spoilers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal the ending of the book in the synopsis; do not worry about 'spoiling' the ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agent or editor doesn't want to know what happens, they will not read the synopsis until after reading the book; therefore, include the ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce your central characters and explain motivations, conflicts, relationships, and reasons readers should care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid listing minor details that aren't important or giving detailed physical descriptions of minor elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tense and Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: Use present tense, third person for book synopses; memoir synopses should be past tense, first person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the manuscript is written in first person, write the synopsis in present-tense third person (except memoirs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense and Hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a strong hook and create intrigue; the synopsis should be interesting, not just accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't have to write thrillers to create suspense. Tease the reader and make them want to know more; dialogue in a synopsis can be effective (example: a synopsis that read like a novel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the voice/style of your synopsis to the style of your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your book is funny, write a funny synopsis; if literary, be highbrow — the synopsis should reflect the book's tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow and Transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure paragraphs flow smoothly and transitions are natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave paragraphs together carefully so transitions don't draw attention to themselves, similar to the way you'd craft transitions in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents and editors use the synopsis as a sign of your professionalism and of whether your book is worth reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't take shortcuts or be lazy when writing a synopsis; craft it as carefully as your book to improve your chances with agents/editors.
